overall: Board violated the OML by posting meeting notices only to its website without adopting that as an alternate posting method; Committee violated it by posting no notices. Minutes-posting and records allegations declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board did not post notice of its meetings, including how the public could attend, and posted only to the Collaborative's website.
allegations.key_passage: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting notice of its meetings only to the Collaborative’s website.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Finance Committee did not post notice of its meetings, including how the public could attend.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to post notice of its meetings.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board and Committee did not post their meeting minutes online and that Board minutes were not timely posted to the website.
allegations.key_passage: Similarly, we decline to review allegations that the Board and Committee did not post their meeting minutes to a website.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a fee estimate was given for a public records request seeking committee communications, including emails between members.
allegations.key_passage: Because the allegation in the complaint regarding a request for communications concerns compliance with the Public Records Law rather than the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law by the Board and Committee
Committee to create minutes for as many meetings as possible
Committee to publicly release any emails in which members deliberated outside a noticed meeting
Committee to certify compliance to the AG within 90 days of the letter
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s and Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board and Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
